title: Instruments on instruments: PER factored, term registries and the valuation memo
description: These claims turn the archive's instruments on themselves: PER factored with the minimality stated as a claim about instrument access, an audit of what each instrument does to the standing of what it measures, data interconnect by derivation, and a missing detector for claim substitution under intact attribution. They include the Term-State Registry's twelve-month failure conditions, the term index plan, relay-traversal and disclosure-battery tests, and matched-pair addresses for the Negative of the Negative. The valuation memo and Semantic Economy Valuation 001 state their own collapse and falsification conditions.

(a) No term transitions from ORPHANED to ATTRIBUTED through provenance coupling deployment — meaning the repair mechanism does not work.

(b) No term transitions from DISSOLVED to SEEDED through rename and re-deposit — meaning dissolution is irreversible regardless of intervention.

An estimated 200-300 coined concepts exist across 841+ deposits without a unified index. Once built, the index becomes:

- A retrieval surface (each term becomes a searchable node)
- A density map (which terms cluster, which are orphaned)
- A versioning base (new deposits append; the initial build is the hard part)

- A measure of the archive's actual vocabulary (what it has coined vs. what it thinks it has coined)
